title: Hybrid eviction safeguards for batched KV allocations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Continuous batching and aggressive GPU memory packing increase pressure on the KV cache. Existing eviction strategies (pure LRU or TTL) either evict hot prefixes prematurely during workload bursts or retain stale prefixes that waste precious GPU memory. This ticket designs and implements a hybrid eviction policy (LRU + adaptive TTL + prefix-awareness) with formal correctness guarantees for prefix-scoped reads and a testable emulator to prevent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Safety invariant: no returned KV entry may be younger than its recorded insertion epoch (no causality inversion) - verified by unit tests.
Prefix-consistency: once a prefix key is evicted, subsequent requests that require that prefix must either miss or rebuild state; no stale cached prefix responses allowed.
Memory accounting: GPU-resident KV usage reported by runtime matches allocator metrics within 2% under steady-state; dump to console and perf dashboard.
Latency/regressions: end-to-end median tail latency impact under representative continuous-batching load is <5% compared to baseline (no new policy) for 95th percentile requests.
Throughput: batching throughput should not decrease by more than 3% under peak load after enabling adaptive TTL heuristics.
Observability: new eviction events instrumented and visible in Console (per-prefix eviction rate, eviction reason distribution: LRU/TTL/pressure) and tied to alerts.
Rollout: feature gated and rolled out to 10% of traffic, validated in staging, then to production with a canary phase and automatic rollback on evictions-per-second > expected threshold.
Test coverage: unit tests, integration tests with eviction-emulator, and a synthetic workload that reproduces prefix-churn pattern included in CI.
design_notes: Policy summary: implement a three-factor eviction score: score = alpha*recency_rank + beta*(1 - normalized_ttl_remaining) + gamma*prefix_penalty. Tunable weights alpha/beta/gamma exposed as runtime flags and Console knobs.

Prefix-aware accounting: track per-prefix resident token count and last-accessed-epoch. Eviction chooses entries by sorted score but enforces a minimum live-window per prefix when prefix is currently being extended by in-flight batches.

Adaptive TTL: TTL is inferred from observed access pattern for a key/prefix (exponential moving average of inter-access intervals). For cold keys TTL decays to base_ttl, for hot keys TTL extends up to max_ttl but is bounded by memory pressure heuristics.

Concurrency model: eviction decisions operate against a snapshot of the allocator's state to avoid races with continuous batching writes. Writers append to an epoch buffer and then publish the epoch atomically; evictor only considers entries with epoch <= publish_epoch - 1.

Correctness guarantees: define epoch monotonicity for writes and eviction to ensure no read-after-evict inconsistency. The design prohibits evicting an entry that has outstanding read promises in the batching pipeline by consulting the in-flight batch registry.

GPU memory optimization: use slab-aligned allocations to reduce fragmentation and implement a small 'emergency stash' region for partial vector KV entries to avoid OOM during compaction; stash is reclaimed preferentially.

Fallbacks: when eviction pressure is extreme, policy falls back to prefix-priority eviction (sacrificing small prefixes to preserve long-lived session prefixes) and triggers an immediate telemetry event for operator action.
Runtime flags and Console: expose alpha/beta/gamma, base_ttl, max_ttl, prefix_min_live_window_ms, and stash_size_bytes via config and console slider for experiments.

Related trade-offs: heavier prefix-awareness protects session continuity but may increase fragmentation. Adaptive TTL reduces unnecessary evictions but risks retaining stale entries if access patterns suddenly change; mitigations include a short cold-check period after long idle windows.
testing_plan: Unit tests: eviction scoring, epoch snapshot behavior, prefix minimum live-window enforcement, stash reclamation logic.

Eviction-emulator: extend existing emulator to model continuous batching and in-flight promises. Run synthetic workloads: bursty prefix-churn, many short prefixes, long-lived conversations, and mixed loads.
Integration tests: deploy to staging runtime with real GPU types (A10G and H100) and run perf scripts; validate memory reporting and tail latencies.
Chaos tests: simulate slow writers, delayed publish epochs, and sudden surge of prefixes to ensure safeties prevent stale reads and OOMs.
Benchmarking: measure token throughput, median and 95th/99th tail latencies, eviction rate, and GPU memory fragmentation before/after.
Regression detection: add CI job that replays recorded production traces and fails if eviction discrepancy or correctness invariant violated.
Manual QA: UX/Console verification for new metrics and canary rollout observations.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind kv.hybrid_eviction_enabled and runtime flag for scoring weights.
Stage 1: Internal staging environment with daily synthetic load for 72 hours.
Stage 2: Canary: 1% production traffic (non-critical workspaces) for 24 hours, monitor telemetry (evictions/sec, mmu pressure, latency).
Stage 3: Ramp: 10% traffic for 48 hours, apply weight adjustments if necessary.
Stage 4: Full rollout with 1-hour watch and 6-hourly checks for 72 hours. Auto-rollback if eviction rate > threshold or customer-impact metrics breach SLOs.
Operator runbook: steps to disable hybrid eviction, gather debug dumps (allocator map, in-flight batch registry, eviction logs), and contact runtime-oncall.

2025-02-18 Diego Mendez: Added design sketch for epoch-based snapshot and in-flight batch registry checks. Need Perf team numbers to tune alpha/beta/gamma.
2025-02-22 Priya Nambiar: Reviewed design; requested explicit invariants for prefix-consistency and a formal proof sketch; suggested adding small emergency stash to avoid OOMs during compaction.

2025-02-25 Diego Mendez: Implemented eviction-emulator extension (branch: feature/eng/ENG-21347-emulator). Preliminary results: 18% fewer prefix rebuilds on bursty workloads vs LRU-only. Pushed initial test coverage.

2025-02-27 Perf team (Ethan Zhao): Measured 3.8% median latency increase and 1.1% throughput reduction on an H100 cluster with default weights (alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1). Suggest lowering alpha to 0.5 for burst workloads.

2025-03-01 Diego Mendez: Addressed concurrency edge where a write published during eviction could be considered for eviction. Added publish_epoch-1 snapshot rule and unit tests. Preparing PR for review.
